# Finding the Antiderivative of ∫ -x^5·sin(3x) dx

## Method: Tabular Integration by Parts

I'll use the tabular method, differentiating the polynomial and integrating the trig function:

| Derivatives of u = -x⁵ | Integrals of dv = sin(3x)dx | Sign |
|---|---|---|
| -x⁵ | -cos(3x)/3 | + |
| -5x⁴ | -sin(3x)/9 | − |
| -20x³ | cos(3x)/27 | + |
| -60x² | sin(3x)/81 | − |
| -120x | -cos(3x)/243 | + |
| -120 | -sin(3x)/729 | − |

## Computing Each Term

**Term 1:** (-x⁵)(-cos(3x)/3) = x⁵·cos(3x)/3

**Term 2:** −(−5x⁴)(−sin(3x)/9) = −5x⁴·sin(3x)/9

**Term 3:** (−20x³)(cos(3x)/27) = −20x³·cos(3x)/27

**Term 4:** −(−60x²)(sin(3x)/81) = 60x²·sin(3x)/81 = 20x²·sin(3x)/27

**Term 5:** (−120x)(−cos(3x)/243) = 120x·cos(3x)/243 = 40x·cos(3x)/81

**Term 6:** −(−120)(−sin(3x)/729) = −120·sin(3x)/729 = −40·sin(3x)/243

## Verification (Differentiating back)

Collecting sin(3x) terms after differentiation:
-(-x⁵) + (-20x³/9 + 20x³/9) + (40x/27 − 40x/27) = **−x⁵** ✓

Collecting cos(3x) terms:
(5x⁴/3 − 5x⁴/3) + (−20x²/9 + 20x²/9) + (40/81 − 40/81) = **0** ✓

The result differentiates to −x⁵·sin(3x). ✓

## Final Answer

<answer>x**5*cos(3*x)/3 - 5*x**4*sin(3*x)/9 - 20*x**3*cos(3*x)/27 + 20*x**2*sin(3*x)/27 + 40*x*cos(3*x)/81 - 40*sin(3*x)/243 + C</answer>
